note: Viscosity of one standard soda-lime-silica glass, NBS Standard Glass No. 710, measured at NBS and seven other laboratories. The Fulcher constants are the combined fit to Laboratory A's five samples (Table 4), log10 η in poise with T in °C, fitted from 560 to 1400 °C; viscosity in Pa·s is poise / 10. Fixed points are the ASTM softening, annealing and strain points in Table 10, averaged over the laboratories that measured them (Avg column). Studio temperatures are typical practice, not measured for this glass. `fitted` is their Table 5 (log10 poise, °C), which this fit reproduces within 3 °C.

source.label: Napolitano and Hawkins, Viscosity of a standard soda-lime-silica glass, J. Res. NBS 68A (1964) 439

points.label: melting
points.definition: 10 Pa·s: runny enough to fine out bubbles

points.label: working
points.definition: 1000 Pa·s: stiff enough to hold a shape on the pipe

points.label: softening
points.definition: Littleton point: a hanging fibre stretches under its own weight

points.label: strain
points.definition: stress takes hours to relax; below it, nothing moves

studio.label: furnace
studio.note: a studio furnace held for gathering (typical, unverified)

studio.label: lehr
studio.note: soaked at the annealing point, then cooled slowly past the strain point

maxwell.note: Infinite-frequency shear modulus, about 30 GPa, used by Zanotto (1998) to turn viscosity into a relaxation time τ = η / G∞.

source.label: Zanotto, Do cathedral glasses flow?, Am. J. Phys. 66 (1998) 392
